events: The Act of Supremacy
Henry VIII is declared supreme head of the Church of England.
The Book of Common Prayer
Cranmer’s first Prayer Book. A second and more Reformed book follows in 1552.
The Oxford martyrs
Under Mary, Latimer and Ridley are burned at Oxford in 1555. Cranmer follows in 1556.
The Elizabethan Settlement
The Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity restore the Prayer Book.
The Thirty-Nine Articles
Agreed by Convocation and made law in 1571.
Hooker’s Laws
The first books of Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity.
Hampton Court
James I meets the bishops and the Puritan petitioners. The new Bible of 1611 follows.
The Synod of Dort
British divines sit at Dort among the Reformed churches.
Laud at Canterbury
William Laud becomes Archbishop of Canterbury.
Civil war
King and Parliament go to war. The presses pour out sermons and pamphlets.
The Westminster Assembly
Divines called by Parliament meet at Westminster to reform the church.
The king executed
Charles I is beheaded. England becomes a commonwealth.
The Great Ejection
Under the Act of Uniformity some two thousand ministers leave their livings.
The Pilgrim’s Progress
Bunyan’s allegory was written in Bedford jail.
Toleration
The Toleration Act allows Dissenters their own worship. The Nonjurors refuse the new oaths.
Aldersgate Street
John Wesley’s heart is “strangely warmed.” Field preaching begins the next year.
Wesley dies
The Methodist societies he led soon become a church of their own.
The Oxford Movement
Keble’s Assize Sermon and the Tracts for the Times. Pusey joins the cause.
